title: Guided Speculative Inference for Efficient Test-Time Alignment of LLMs
claim: A cheap draft model proposes candidates that are scored and accepted if good enough; otherwise the expensive model resamples.
layout: Single flowchart, left-to-right, accept/reject boxes at right, color legend bottom-left
description: A left-to-right flowchart of one reasoning step of the method. Input x feeds a green draft-model sampling box, y_i^S ~ pi_S. From there, three branches compute the target log-probability (blue), the reward (orange), and the draft log-probability (green). These merge into a gray box that defines the tilted reward r~_i = (r + (1/beta) log pi_B/pi_S)(y_i^S). A red S-BoN box selects the index i*. Arrows then split into a pink 'Accept' panel at top right and a larger pink 'Reject' panel at bottom right. The Accept panel holds the test r~ >= u and outputs y^S_{i*}. The Reject panel stacks target-model sampling, reward scoring, a second S-BoN and the output y^B_{i*}. A yellow legend at bottom left maps colors to draft model, target model, reward model and S-BoN.
caption: Guided Speculative Inference workflow for one reasoning step. A sample $y^S_{i^*}$ generated from the draft model $\pi_S$ is selected with soft best-of-$n$ (S-BoN) with parameter $\beta$ from the tilted rewards $\tilde{r}_i$. If its reward lies above a threshold $u$ it is accepted. Otherwise, it is rejected, which triggers resampling from the target model $\pi_B$ with soft best-of-$n$.
abstract: We propose Guided Speculative Inference (GSI), a novel algorithm for efficient reward-guided decoding in large language models. GSI combines soft best-of-$n$ test-time scaling with a reward model $r(x,y)$ and speculative samples from a small auxiliary model $Ï_S(y\mid x)$. We provably approximate both the optimal tilted policy $Ï_{Î²,B}(y\mid x) \propto Ï_B(y\mid x)\exp(Î²\,r(x,y))$ of soft best-of-$n$ under the base model $Ï_B$, as well as the expected reward under the optimal policy. In experiments on reasoning benchmarks (MATH500, OlympiadBench, Minerva Math, MMLU-STEM, GSM8K) and across different model families, our method achieves higher accuracy than standard soft best-of-$n$ with $Ï_S$ and reward-guided speculative decoding (Liao et al., 2025), and in certain settings even outperforms soft best-of-$n$ with $Ï_B$, while reducing end-to-end latency by up to $28\%$. The code is available at https://github.com/j-geuter/GSI .
